content:
Athapookalam Competition 2026

Time: 10:00 AM - 11:30 AM

Venue: Main Auditorium Foyer

Coordinator: Arts Club Committee

Inter-departmental traditional floral carpet (Athapookalam) designing competition showcasing artistic creativity, traditional patterns, floral arrangement, symmetry, and Kerala's cultural heritage.

Competition Details

  • Duration: 90 minutes
  • Plot Size: 5 feet × 5 feet
  • Maximum Teams: 2 teams per department
  • Team Size: Maximum 8 participants per team
  • Theme: Traditional Kerala-inspired floral design

General Rules

  1. Each department can register a maximum of 2 teams.
  2. Each team must have a maximum of 8 participants.
  3. Only registered team members are allowed to participate in the competition.
  4. Team members must report to the venue at least 15 minutes before the starting time.
  5. The competition will begin exactly at 10:00 AM.
  6. Teams arriving after the competition begins may be allowed to participate only with the permission of the coordinators.
  7. Each team will be provided with an assigned 5 feet × 5 feet plot.
  8. Teams must complete their Pookalam within the allotted 90 minutes.
  9. All designing and decoration work must be completed before 11:30 AM.
  10. No team will be allowed to continue working after the official closing time.
  11. Participants must maintain cleanliness and avoid disturbing other teams.
  12. Teams are responsible for keeping their assigned area clean throughout the competition.

Allowed Materials

  • Only fresh natural flowers are permitted.
  • Green leaves and other naturally available plant materials may be used.
  • Permitted flowers include Thumba, Chethi, Mukkutti, Kakka Poovu, Marigold (Jamanthi), Rose, and Jasmine.
  • Small variations of naturally available flowers may be permitted at the discretion of the coordinators.
  • Chalk may be used only for making the initial outline or marking the design.
  • Natural leaves may be used for borders and decorative elements.

Prohibited Materials

  • Artificial flowers and plastic flowers are not allowed.
  • Plastic sheets, plastic decorations, thermocol, glitter, and synthetic decorative materials are not permitted.
  • Paint, poster colour, artificial colouring powder, and chemical dyes are not allowed.
  • Ready-made decorative items cannot be placed inside the Pookalam.
  • Printed pictures, photographs, banners, and electronic decorations are prohibited.
  • Adhesives, glue, tape, or other artificial fixing materials should not be used.
  • Participants must not use materials that may permanently damage the floor or competition area.

Design Rules

  1. The Pookalam must be created entirely within the assigned 5 feet × 5 feet area.
  2. The design should reflect the traditional character of an Athapookalam.
  3. Teams are encouraged to maintain proper symmetry, balance, and neatness.
  4. The use of flowers should contribute to the overall artistic appearance of the design.
  5. The design should not obstruct or extend into another team's assigned area.
  6. Teams must create the design during the competition period; pre-arranged finished sections are not permitted.
  7. All flowers and materials brought by the team may be inspected by the coordinators.

Judging Criteria

  • Creativity & Originality: 25 marks
  • Traditional Appeal: 20 marks
  • Flower Arrangement & Colour Combination: 20 marks
  • Symmetry & Design: 15 marks
  • Neatness & Finishing: 10 marks
  • Overall Presentation: 10 marks

Total: 100 marks

Judging Guidelines

  • Judges will evaluate the completed Pookalam after the competition ends.
  • The decision of the judging panel will be final.
  • Teams may be penalized for using prohibited materials.
  • Designs extending beyond the assigned area may receive a penalty.
  • Late completion may result in disqualification or reduction of marks as decided by the coordinators.
  • Cleanliness and proper use of the allotted space will be considered during evaluation.

Important Instructions

  • Participants should bring their required flowers and permitted materials with them.
  • Teams should carry their own containers or bags for transporting flowers and leaves.
  • Participants should avoid wasting flowers and other natural materials.
  • Any dispute should be immediately brought to the attention of the Arts Club Committee.
  • Participants must follow instructions given by the coordinators and volunteers.
  • Any attempt to disturb or damage another team's Pookalam may result in disqualification.
  • The organizing committee reserves the right to modify minor arrangements when necessary for the smooth conduct of the competition.

Prize & Recognition

The winning teams will be selected based on the final judging score. Prizes and certificates may be awarded to the winners and participating teams according to the official Onam celebration guidelines.
